title: The Millennium
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Millennium refers to the reign described in Revelation 20 and the biblical hope of Christ’s rule over His enemies. Faithful Christians differ on details, so this doctrine should be handled with humility under Scripture.
summary: The Millennium refers to the reign described in Revelation 20 and the biblical hope of Christ’s rule over His enemies. Faithful Christians differ on details, so this doctrine should be handled with humility under Scripture.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the reigning King. Whatever view believers hold about the Millennium, Scripture calls them to confess that Christ reigns, will defeat His enemies, and will bring His kingdom to completion.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Revelation 20 speaks of a thousand-year reign, and Christians have understood its timing and nature in different ways. This requires humility and carefulness.

The central truth must not be lost: Christ reigns, Satan is limited by God, the saints belong to the victorious Lord, and evil will be finally judged.

This doctrine should not become a test of Christian fellowship where Scripture allows room for faithful disagreement. Believers must not make their timeline system more central than Christ Himself.

The Millennium points to the certainty of Christ’s kingdom and the defeat of His enemies. The King will reign until every enemy is under His feet.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Eschatology can become divisive when secondary details are treated as though they are the Gospel itself. This doctrine teaches conviction with humility.

The church needs clarity about Christ’s reign more than pride about a timeline. The hope of Scripture is not winning arguments, but the triumph of Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Study Revelation 20 carefully and humbly. Hold your convictions under Scripture, respect faithful believers who differ on difficult details, and keep Christ’s reign, holiness, mission, and hope at the center.
